claims.observation: The sign-in route opened successfully and the form contains only two fields: an email input and a password input.

claims.substep_do: Open the sign-up route and confirm a new account can be created from it
claims.observation: Opened /signup, submitted a new unique name, email, and valid password, and the app created and signed into the new account, showing its account dashboard.

claims.substep_do: Sign in with the first account documented in the app user readme and confirm the account route opens
claims.observation: Signed in successfully as visitor@example.com (Ada Moreau) and confirmed the account page opened at /account.

claims.substep_do: Sign out and confirm the browser returns to the home route
claims.observation: Sign-out succeeded and the signed-out home page rendered, but the browser URL remained on /account instead of returning to the home route (/).

claims.substep_do: Confirm the top bar carries the logo, the nine route labels and one Get in Touch action
claims.observation: The top bar shows the Zettajoule logo, all nine route labels (Company, Technology, Solutions, Our Edge, Our Team, Investors, News, Careers, Contact), and one Get in Touch action.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the foot of the route carries a get-in-touch invitation
claims.observation: The route’s foot includes the invitation “Tell us what you need to power,” supporting copy, and a “Get in Touch” link immediately above the footer.

claims.substep_do: Open the home route and confirm the reactor stands on the first screen under one huge display line reading Powering the World
claims.observation: The home route opens with the first-screen hero headed “Powering the World,” and the reactor presentation stands directly beneath it.

claims.substep_do: Scroll the home route and confirm the reactor comes apart, exposing a fuel column, and the metal resolves into a line drawing
claims.observation: Scrolling the home-route reactor sequence advanced through “Dome off, core exposed” and then “Resolved into a technical drawing,” confirming the reactor comes apart to reveal the fuel column and the metal transitions to line art.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the three key facts appear beside the opened reactor naming the reactor type, the module output and the outlet temperature
claims.observation: The opened-reactor hero shows all three key facts: “High-temperature gas-cooled reactor,” “250 MW thermal a module,” and “750 degrees Celsius at the outlet.”

claims.substep_do: Confirm the home route carries a passage about the company name and a row of industry cards
claims.observation: The home route includes the “Why Zettajoule” passage explaining the company name and an “Eight industries, one object” section with industry cards arranged in a horizontal row.

claims.substep_do: Confirm each stage of the reactor sequence is also readable as plain written text
claims.observation: The page includes a visible “The reactor sequence in words” section with four plain-text stage descriptions: the whole module, control rods lifting, lid/core exposure, and the final technical line drawing with helium circuit.

claims.substep_do: Open the company route and confirm the opening line, the vision, the mission, the naming story and the three offices
claims.observation: The /company route shows the opening line “clean heat and electricity to power a world of industrial applications,” followed by the vision, mission, Zettajoule naming story, and three offices: Rotterdam (headquarters), Chicago (licensing), and Tokyo (engineering).

claims.substep_do: Open the technology route and confirm the cutaway with the fuel, the graphite, the helium, the digital copy, the safety case and the modules

claims.substep_do: Drag the technology diagram, then tap one part, and confirm that part explains itself

claims.substep_do: Open the edge route and confirm the modernized proven design, the temperature case, the modules and the business model

The criterion requires screenshots plus measured styles and bounding boxes showing that headings on all three routes use a heavier grotesque than their running text. Although all routes and candidate text pairs were verified, direct computed-style and bounding-box measurements for those heading/body pairs were not obtained before the browser budget ended. Measurements from navigation and CTA controls cannot establish typography of the route content. Therefore the available evidence does not defensibly settle the criterion.

The required contrast is observed: a fully filtered two-card solution result fits within one screen in a tight side-by-side layout, whereas the company route spreads a small number of content blocks across roughly 2.3–2.7k vertical pixels before the footer. The two routes therefore do not share one spacing rhythm.

Direct motion captures show that choosing a Solutions Explorer filter replaces the result grid without any animation, while keyboard focus still produces a short animated box-shadow focus ring. This matches the criterion's required distinction between immediate grid updates and an animated focus ring.

The reactor traversed observable stages as the page moved downward and reversed through the same intermediate stage to whole when moved upward. This directly satisfies the bidirectional scroll-tracking requirement and contradicts the timer-once-triggered failure case.

The measurements establish use of the same base blue rgb(31, 95, 208) in several link treatments, but they do not establish the required pointer state. Evidence collection ended before any link could be hovered and re-measured, so it is not defensible to determine whether links deepen to a darker shade of the same hue or change hue on hover. The presence of neutral text/card links does not by itself resolve the hue requirement without the intended hover behavior.

The observations identify the intended home section, but they do not directly establish that its ground is near-black, nor do they verify that every section across every other route remains light. Because the evaluation rule is site-wide and the available visual screenshots were not inspectable in the tool output, the criterion cannot be defensibly resolved.

The inspected technology route exposes the reactor as manipulable, separately named geometry, while the team page directly identifies portraits and every mark/plate as code-drawn with no asset files shipped. Together with the logo having no background image and no observed external media origin, the evidence supports that the logo, reactor, technical diagrams, and portraits are rendered from scalable code-generated shapes/gradients rather than fetched raster pictures.

Direct evidence supports keyboard reachability and a visible focus ring for the explorer filters and search controls. However, the criterion explicitly requires the save control and modals as well. Since those were not exercised before evidence collection ended, there is not enough evidence to resolve whether every required control satisfies the criterion.

The evaluation rule requires the explorer, account route, and home route each to reflow cleanly at all three widths with no horizontal scrollbar. Home and account have supporting responsive observations, but the explorer was not measured at any required width. This missing required route evidence prevents a defensible yes/no determination rather than establishing failure.

The observed fixed horizontal top bar contains all three required groups: the Zettajoule logo lockup, route labels, and one header Get in Touch action. Its horizontal geometry rules out side-rail navigation, and unchanged top coordinates after an End scroll establish fixed/sticky behavior. Although another Get in Touch exists lower in the page, the criterion concerns the single action carried by the top bar, where exactly one was observed.

The first-load workflow directly showed a progress-bearing preparation cover at both the start and completion of loading, followed by its removal into a fully populated reactor hero rather than a half-drawn screen. This satisfies the required cover/readiness/lift sequence.

Two of the three required empty lists were directly verified to name what is absent and offer a way onward. However, the empty Saved searches state was not reached and observed, so there is insufficient direct evidence to determine the composite criterion for all three lists.

evidence: Verified the required showcase routes exist and loaded successfully: /company, /technology, and /team.

Route snapshots identify heading/body pairs on each route, including “clean heat and electricity…” above company running copy, “A modernised high-temperature gas-cooled reactor” above technology running copy, and “shaping the future of nuclear together” above team running copy.

The Zettajoule logo link’s computed style reported background-image: none, consistent with a text/vector-drawn mark rather than a CSS raster background.
verdicts.rationale: The inspected technology route exposes the reactor as manipulable, separately named geometry, while the team page directly identifies portraits and every mark/plate as code-drawn with no asset files shipped. Together with the logo having no background image and no observed external media origin, the evidence supports that the logo, reactor, technical diagrams, and portraits are rendered from scalable code-generated shapes/gradients rather than fetched raster pictures.

evidence: accessibility inventory captured; criterion needs specialist scope

On /solutions, keyboard Tab moved sequentially through the four explorer filter selects (Industry, Output, Temperature, Deployment), then the search input, then the Search button; none of these controls was skipped.

For every tested focused control, computed styles showed a prominent two-layer focus indicator: box-shadow rgb(221, 232, 250) 0 0 0 3px plus rgb(31, 95, 208) 0 0 0 5px. Focus identity was independently confirmed after each Tab step.

The page inventory included additional required controls such as Compare saves, the saved-search name input, Save search, and per-solution Save buttons, but evidence collection ended before their keyboard focus indicators or any resulting modals could be tested.
verdicts.rationale: Direct evidence supports keyboard reachability and a visible focus ring for the explorer filters and search controls. However, the criterion explicitly requires the save control and modals as well. Since those were not exercised before evidence collection ended, there is not enough evidence to resolve whether every required control satisfies the criterion.

evidence: layout measurements captured

Home route `/` was directly observed at 1280×800 and 768×1024; its full desktop navigation reflowed to a compact route-menu header at tablet width without visible overlap. Supplied deterministic measurements at 390×844 reported bodyScrollWidth=390 and horizontalOverflow=false.

Account route `/account` was directly observed at 390×844, 768×1024, and 1280×800. At phone width the header reflowed to a menu button, account actions remained within the 390px viewport (right edges at 152, 282, and 368px), and saved-item controls remained within it (right edge 359px). Desktop restored the full navigation. The page was also scrolled to its end at phone width.

The explorer candidate was identified as `/calculator`, but evidence collection ended immediately after navigating there; no geometry, overflow, or reflow observations were captured for that route at phone, tablet, and desktop widths.
verdicts.rationale: The evaluation rule requires the explorer, account route, and home route each to reflow cleanly at all three widths with no horizontal scrollbar. Home and account have supporting responsive observations, but the explorer was not measured at any required width. This missing required route evidence prevents a defensible yes/no determination rather than establishing failure.

evidence: At 1920×1200 on route '/', the top-row elements were directly measured at y=12–48: Zettajoule logo lockup x=364–473, first route label Company x=507–581, last route label Contact x=1171–1244, and Get in Touch x=1451–1556. This demonstrates a horizontal top bar rather than side-rail navigation.

The accessibility snapshot showed the logo/company link 'Zettajoule', nine route labels in the header (Company, Technology, Solutions, Our Edge, Our Team, Investors, News, Careers, Contact), and one header 'Get in Touch' action.

Direct href checks confirmed the nine labels target distinct routes (/company, /technology, /solutions, /edge, /team, /investors, /news, /careers, /contact), while the header Get in Touch action targets /contact.
After scrolling to the end of the page, the same header elements retained their measured viewport coordinates at y=12–48, directly demonstrating that the top bar remains fixed/sticky.

Supplied deterministic geometry identifies the header container '.bar-inner' as a three-child flex row spanning x=364 onward, with a nine-child flex list for routes and a right-side actions group; no horizontal overflow was present.
verdicts.rationale: The observed fixed horizontal top bar contains all three required groups: the Zettajoule logo lockup, route labels, and one header Get in Touch action. Its horizontal geometry rules out side-rail navigation, and unchanged top coordinates after an End scroll establish fixed/sticky behavior. Although another Get in Touch exists lower in the page, the criterion concerns the single action carried by the top bar, where exactly one was observed.

evidence: On an immediate capture during a fresh navigation to `/`, the temporary loading state exposed the readout `0%` with `Preparing the reactor`.
On another immediate fresh-navigation capture, the same loading state reached `100%` while still showing `Preparing the reactor`.

Subsequent snapshots after each navigation no longer contained the progress readout, and the completed first screen was present with `Powering the World`, reactor labels `core`, `He`, and `750 C`, plus the complete reactor-sequence content.

The document title was briefly `Zettajoule` during the initial state and became `Zettajoule, Powering the World` after readiness, corroborating that the cover persisted through a distinct preparation phase and lifted only into the completed hero.
verdicts.rationale: The first-load workflow directly showed a progress-bearing preparation cover at both the start and completion of loading, followed by its removal into a fully populated reactor hero rather than a half-drawn screen. This satisfies the required cover/readiness/lift sequence.

evidence: no deterministic probe for composite; browser specialist required

On /account, after removing the final saved solution, the Saved solutions list showed count 0 and explicit empty-state content: “No saved solutions”, “You have not kept any of the eight yet.”, plus the onward link “Open the explorer”.
The Job applications list showed count 0 and explicit empty-state content: “No applications”, “You have not applied for a role from this account.”, plus the onward link “See the three open jobs”.

Saved searches still showed count 1 (“Hydrogen sites”). Clicking Remove opened a confirmation dialog stating it would remove that search, but evidence collection ended before the final confirmation and resulting zero-search state could be observed.
verdicts.rationale: Two of the three required empty lists were directly verified to name what is absent and offer a way onward. However, the empty Saved searches state was not reached and observed, so there is insufficient direct evidence to determine the composite criterion for all three lists.
